# Roadmap

* [Designer app build status](build-status.md) (draft) - Where the build of the designer app stands against the roadmap phases P0-P8: what each phase delivered, measured numbers, known gaps, how to run and test, and what comes next. Updated at the end of every phase.
* [Solver race plan](solver-race-plan.md) - Plan (2026-11-02) and results (2026-11-03) for choosing the fit solver that meets the owner's 5-second re-fit target. Raced on the GTX 1650 in NVIDIA Warp: today's local/global method on the GPU won (5 ms per step against 820 ms on the CPU; cutouts to the accuracy bar in 2-4 s, pose shapes settled in 1-2 s); Newton, L-BFGS, VBD and a multi-level V-cycle lost. Frictionless, the garment's placement along the body is nearly free and no solver pins it within 5 s; with friction on re-fits (owner, same day) poses still end 1.2-2.2 mm mean from the reference, the sleeve turning round the arm most; an early result of 0.3-0.6 mm was a bug (random normals on points resting on the body).

# Technique

* [Drafted blocks](drafted-blocks.md) (draft) - The project's own leotard blocks, November 2026: drawn from a body's tape measures in true curves with seam joins decided in advance. 17 blocks (six app bodies, eleven adult sizes), all but XXS passing 42 pattern checks; six fitted on their own bodies. Calibrated, unreviewed, not yet in the app.
* [Fit solver realism audit](fit-solver-realism-audit.md) (draft) - November 2026 audit of pipeline/wrap_block.py against public cloth simulators and skin-tight garment research, before any speed work: a sound geometric fit but not a realistic cloth simulation. Fifteen ranked differences, then first-hand results for steps 1-5: the fit settles and holds up on finer meshes and in a heavier simulator, no new physics earned its place, carrying a fit into a pose is the largest error measured, and wrinkles now come from the fit.
* [Fitting a block like the app](fitting-a-block-like-the-app.md) (draft) - November 2026: why drafted blocks fitted badly at the seat and thighs. The drafter's leg cuts had left the purchased block; they are now its own lines scaled to each body, with named, tunable elastic in the fit, fabric that gathers rather than resisting compression, and finished edges. An edit tuned to the app's look and a hard crotch pin were rejected and removed.
* [The flat and 3D link](flat-and-3d-link.md) (draft) - Stage 4 prototype, 2026-11-01: artwork lives on one canvas per cut piece, the garment wears those canvases and the PDF prints them. Round trip exact, seam crossings continuous, export true to scale. Dev-only at /wrap.html; not in the app, and unproven on real fabric.
* [The app's flat pattern against a real block](flat-pattern-against-a-real-block.md) - Measured on 2026-11-01: the young body is nearest block size XS. Total trunk length matches, but the app's flattened pieces follow body bumps, shift the shoulder seam, have a much shorter sleeve with a lower sleeve head, and one uniform ease that is too tight at the waist and too loose at bust and hip.
* [The re-fit in the app (WebGPU) and its tuning page](refit-in-the-app.md) (draft) - November 2026: today's local/global method with friction, ported from the solver race to WebGPU in the app (app/src/fit/), with a dev tuning page at /refit.html to trade speed against accuracy. 2 ms per step on the GTX 1650 (Python's Warp version 6 ms); matches Python to 0.002 mm after a step. A stop rule by window-averaged drift ends cutouts in 30-90 steps; poses keep sliding slowly and run to the step limit (750 steps, about 1.7 s).
* [Refitting after an edit](refitting-after-an-edit.md) (draft) - November 2026: how fast and how accurately a fitted block re-settles after a structural edit such as a cutout, started from the fit already there. First measurement, on one body, of the owner's plan for updating the fit inside the app.
* [Wrapping a flat block onto the body](wrapping-a-flat-block-onto-the-body.md) (draft) - Stage 3 spike, 2026-11-01: a purchased block's flat pieces, seams welded, solved onto the garment surface in about four minutes for five solves. Under 0.1% inside out, zero seam gap, stretch close to the block's intended ease; a neckline cut can reuse the fit, a large leg cut should not. The map is host triangles the app's own renderer can use.
